exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Magnitude of a Sum of Vectors Using the Pythagorean Theorem

question.text: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ is directed due west and $|\mathbf{a}|=16.$ The vector $\mathbf{b}$ is directed vertically up and $|\mathbf{b}|=8.$ Find $|\mathbf{a+b}|.$
question.explanation:
We use the triangle law of addition to add the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$

Notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use Pythagorean theorem as follows:

\begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={|\mathbf{a}|}^2+{|\mathbf{b}|}^2 \\[5pt] &={16}^2+{8}^2 \\[5pt] &=320 \end{align*}

Hence, $|\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{320}=8\sqrt{5}.$

question.text: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ is directed due west and $|\mathbf{a}|=15.$ The vector $\mathbf{b}$ is directed vertically up and $|\mathbf{b}|=9.$ Find the exact value of $|\mathbf{a+b}|.$
question.explanation:
We use the triangle law of addition to add the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$

Notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem as follows:

\begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={|\mathbf{a}|}^2+{|\mathbf{b}|}^2 \\[5pt] &={15}^2+{9}^2 \\[5pt] &=306 \end{align*}

Hence, $|\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{306}= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3\sqrt{34}}.$

question.text: Consider the picture shown above. Find the exact value of $|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|.$
question.explanation:
We use the triangle law of addition for $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$ We can start $\mathbf{a}$ from an arbitrary point on the plane. The resultant goes from the start of $\mathbf{a}$ to the head of $\mathbf{b}.$

Now, in $\bigtriangleup{AHB},$ we have $m\angle{AHB} = 90^\circ,$ $AH = 30\:\textrm{mm},$ and $BH=10\:\textrm{mm}.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives \begin{align*} |\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}| &= AB \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{AH^2+BH^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{30^2+10^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{900 + 100} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{1000} \\[5pt] &= 10\sqrt{10}\:\textrm{mm}. \end{align*}

Therefore, $|\mathbf{a+b}|= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10\sqrt{10}}\:\textrm{mm}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Magnitude of a Sum of Vectors Using the Law of Cosines

question.text: Given the diagram above, where $|\mathbf{a}|=3$ and $|\mathbf{b}|=4$, find the value of $|\mathbf{a+b}|.$
question.explanation:
We use the triangle law for adding the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$

Using the law of cosines, we obtain:

\begin{align*} {|\mathbf{a+b}|}^2 &={\mathbf{|a|}}^2+{\mathbf{|b|}}^2-2\mathbf{|a||b|}\cos ({120}^\circ) \\[5pt] &={3}^2+{4}^2-2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4 \cdot \left(-\dfrac 1 2\right) \\[5pt] &=9+16+12 \\[5pt] &=37 \end{align*}

Hence, $|\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{37}.$

example.title: Calculating the Magnitude of a Sum of Vectors Using the Law of Cosines

question.text: Given the diagram above, where $|\mathbf{a}|=5\sqrt{3}$ and $|\mathbf{b}|=6,$ find the exact value of $|\mathbf{a+b}|.$
question.explanation:
We use the triangle law for adding the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}.$

Using the law of cosines, we obtain

\begin{align*} |\mathbf{a+b}|^2 &= |\mathbf{a}|^2+|\mathbf{b}|^2-2|\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|\cos 150^\circ \\[4pt] &= (5\sqrt{3})^2+6^2-2\cdot (5\sqrt{3})\cdot 6\cdot\!\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\[4pt] &= 75+36+90 \\[4pt] &= 201. \end{align*}

Hence, we get \[ |\mathbf{a+b}| = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\sqrt{201}}. \]
